Title: Trigger Finger: People With Diabetes Are Up To 4 Times More Likely To Get One

Description:
Ever had a finger get stuck bent and then pop straight? That's trigger finger — the tendon that bends your finger swells inside its narrow tunnel and a small nodule catches every time you move it.

People with diabetes are up to 4 times more likely to develop it, and it's also more common after 45 and with rheumatoid arthritis. Repetitive gripping (manual work, tools, even keyboard and mouse use) is a trigger too.

Mild cases often respond to rest and OTC anti-inflammatories. If it's actually locking, a night splint or a steroid injection are the next steps — surgery is only for cases that don't respond to those.

If your finger is locking, get it checked within weeks, not months.
